rubrics.justification: Generally recognizes a poor-quality blastocyst with absent/degenerative ICM and TE, but introduces uncertainty and some inconsistency about expansion stage (1DD vs possible 2DD/collapse) and comments on image features that are not clearly verifiable from a single image.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, oocyte yield, diagnosis, sperm quality, endometrium, BMI, and lifestyle reasonably well, with appropriate emphasis on age and embryo quality as dominant prognostic factors.

Overall logic is sound, but there are internal inconsistencies in the draft discussion (e.g., comments about other embryos/cryostorage not supported by the case, mixed statements on grading, and shifting probability framing). Final conclusions are mostly coherent.

Mostly aligned with standard IVF practice in recommending SET, luteal support, and cautious counseling, but includes some less evidence-based or loosely framed suggestions in the draft discussion (e.g., IVIG/add-ons, broad PGT-A framing) and some grading confusion relative to Gardner criteria.

Provides practical next steps for transfer, follow-up, counseling, and future cycle planning, including SET, luteal support, prenatal optimization, and discussion of PGT-A/stimulation review. Some recommendations remain somewhat generic.
